name: fish
summary: A user-friendly shell implemented around a structured tokenizer/parser, an interactive reader with event hooks and completion, and explicit environment and process execution layers.

features.name: Structured command parser
features.description: The fixed Rust source tokenizes input into a parse tree and evaluates parsed source through parser and execution modules. Fish documentation describes its command, variable, quoting, and expansion language as a distinct shell syntax.
benefits: Makes syntax and command structure available to parsing, completion, and diagnostics
Separates lexical structure from later expansion and execution
costs: Parser, expansion, and evaluation stages must preserve shell-specific semantics
Syntax changes affect interactive tooling as well as batch execution

features.name: Interactive reader and event boundary
features.description: The reader implementation handles character events, prompts, history, completion, repainting, and preexec/postexec/exit hooks. Fish's interactive documentation describes the reader, key bindings, autosuggestions, and completion as interactive shell facilities.
benefits: Integrates editing, completion, history, and hooks around one command reader
Makes user interaction extensible through named events and functions
costs: Event hooks and repainting introduce ordering and reentrancy concerns
Interactive behavior adds state beyond the command language itself

features.name: Environment and process execution boundary
features.description: Fish separates environment state, redirections, job groups, process spawning, and execution in dedicated source modules. The language manual documents variables, pipelines, redirections, and command substitution at the shell boundary.
benefits: Keeps shell variables and process resources explicit across execution paths
Supports pipelines and external commands without conflating them with parsing
costs: OS process, file-descriptor, and signal behavior remain external dependencies
Environment mutation and child-process lifecycle require careful restoration

mathematical_views.question: How does fish source become a parse tree, expanded command, and process or builtin effect?
assumptions: Source is transformed through tokenization, parse-tree construction, expansion, and evaluation
Each stage preserves the information required by later shell semantics
The view abstracts terminal input and OS scheduling

mathematical_views.question: How do character input, completion, history, hooks, repainting, and command execution interact?
assumptions: Reader state is a central mutable resource
Events and reader actions are directed edges to parser or display effects
The graph does not imply that hooks are synchronous in every platform path

benefits: Syntax-aware tooling can share parsed structure
costs: Language evolution must coordinate multiple stages

benefits: Interactive features compose around explicit events
costs: Hooks and redraw state complicate control flow

benefits: Process and variable boundaries are explicit
costs: Platform process semantics remain part of correctness
